title: A Songbook for the Harbor
premise: Ivo Quintana returns to her family's island harbor for her grandmother's eightieth-birthday reunion, dreading the questions about her stalled writing career and failed engagement. To deflect scrutiny, she recruits Theo Marchetti, a visiting marine restorer renting the lighthouse cottage, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake romance deepens into something real just as Ivo learns her powerful uncle plans to sell the lighthouse and evict Theo's restoration project, forcing her to choose between family loyalty and the life she actually wants. When Theo leaves on the last ferry believing she chose duty over him, Ivo must finally claim her voice, her novel, and her heart, winning him back at the winter ferry landing as the season turns.
about_author: Beatrix Villalobos is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse, where she insists every love story deserves weather.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Returning to Quintana Harbor after two years away, Ivo rehearses excuses for her unfinished novel and broken engagement while the ferry cuts through fog. The emotional beat is dread sharpened by homesickness; she realizes she has been hiding in the mainland the way she hides inside unfinished manuscripts.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the Cottage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marine restorer Theo Marchetti unpacks crates of salvaged ship fittings in the lighthouse cottage, racing a grant deadline his benefactor keeps threatening to revoke. He meets Ivo when she mistakes him for a cousin. The beat is wary curiosity between two people guarding their own failures.

chapters.title: Reunion Roster
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the Quintana house, Aunt Marisol distributes the reunion itinerary like battle orders, and Uncle Rafael announces he'll unveil 'the future of the harbor' at the birthday dinner. Ivo's ex-fiancé Daniel RSVPs. The beat is claustrophobia; Ivo invents a boyfriend on the spot to survive Sunday's toast.

chapters.title: Terms of the Lie
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Ivo proposes the fake date to Theo over chowder; he agrees if she'll help him document the lighthouse's original lens for his grant. They negotiate rules like a contract. The beat is playful tension masking mutual loneliness, each recognizing a fellow person mid-escape.

chapters.title: First Light, First Lie
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the clambake, Ivo introduces Theo, who performs charmingly well—too well. Grandmother Elena studies them both with unsettling warmth. Daniel corners Ivo about closure. The beat is the first crack: the lie feels easier than truth, which frightens her more than exposure would.

chapters.title: The Lens Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo shows Ivo the Fresnel lens at dawn, confessing that his restoration career collapsed after a scandal he didn't cause. Ivo admits her novel is 40,000 words of avoidance. The beat is reciprocal vulnerability; intimacy begins not with touch but with traded confessions.

chapters.title: Rafael's Blueprint
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo discovers Rafael's development plans: the lighthouse converted to a private event venue, the keeper's cottage leased to investors, Theo's project terminated. Rafael offers her a paid role as 'heritage consultant.' The beat is betrayal; the family legacy she mourned is being sold by its own steward.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At Elena's birthday dinner, Theo defends the lighthouse's history so passionately that the table goes quiet—and under it, he takes Ivo's hand. The fake date stops feeling fake by dessert. The beat is the point of no return, witnessed by everyone except the two people living it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A storm grounds all ferries, stranding Theo and forcing the extended family under one roof. Forced proximity strips performance away: they cook together, argue about books, and nearly kiss before Cousin Pia interrupts. The beat is aching suspension, desire outrunning the agreed rules.

chapters.title: The Kiss That Wasn't in the Contract
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. After the storm clears, Theo and Ivo kiss in the boathouse and immediately renegotiate everything—or avoid doing so, agreeing to 'see where it goes' without naming it. The beat is giddy denial; both know the arrangement has expired but neither will say the word real.

chapters.title: Pia Knows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pia confronts Ivo: she saw them kiss and knows the relationship began as theater, and she's furious at being cast as an extra in Ivo's story. The beat is guilt; Ivo realizes her habit of managing appearances has cost her the sisterhood she came home for.

chapters.title: Daniel at the Dock
chapters.summary: Daniel's brief POV shifting to Ivo's. Daniel asks Ivo to try again, offering stability, a city apartment, distance from family chaos. Ivo almost says yes out of exhaustion. The beat is temptation of the smaller life—the safe second chance that isn't actually hers.

chapters.title: The Grant Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's funding is officially revoked, engineered by Rafael's lawyers to clear the cottage. Theo, burned before by institutions, assumes Ivo knew and says things he can't take back. The beat is rupture; old wounds convert new information into old betrayals.

chapters.title: Chapters Left Unsent
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reads Theo's grant proposal and finds her own unpublished manuscript quoted in his vision statement—he'd been her reader all along. She writes him a letter explaining Rafael's coercion, then can't decide whether sending it is honesty or another performance. The beat is paralysis at the threshold of courage.

chapters.title: Elena's Logbook
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Grandmother Elena gives Ivo her late husband's lighthouse logbooks, revealing that Elena herself once chose duty over a love who left on the last ferry—and regretted it for sixty years. The beat is inheritance of warning; the past hands Ivo the map she's been refusing to read.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the family council, Rafael demands unanimous approval of the venue plan. Ivo stands and reads aloud from the logbooks, arguing the lighthouse belongs to the harbor's memory, not its market value. The vote splits. The beat is open rebellion; invisibility ends here, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Beaten down by the scandal resurfacing and Ivo's silence, Theo packs his tools and boards the last autumn ferry without saying goodbye. Ivo arrives at the dock four minutes too late, letter still unsent. The beat is devastation; the lie's final cost comes due in full view of the water.

chapters.title: Wintering
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Weeks pass. Ivo finishes her novel in the lighthouse cottage, sends it to an agent, and publicly files to designate the lighthouse a protected landmark, estranging half the family. The beat is grief transmuted into work; she builds the life she'd have shared with him, alone.

chapters.title: What Rafael Buried
chapters.summary: Ivo and Pia's alternating POV. Pia uncovers proof that Rafael falsified the ownership transfer years ago and blackmailed the previous grant committee—including the scandal that ruined Theo. The sisters reconcile over the evidence. The beat is alliance; found family reassembles around truth instead of blood loyalty.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the landmark hearing, Ivo testifies, Elena corroborates, and Pia presents the documents. Rafael's scheme collapses; he exits the family rather than face it. The beat is cathartic justice tempered by sorrow—Ivo wins the lighthouse but loses the illusion of a whole family.

chapters.title: Return Passage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reads about the hearing in a maritime journal, learns the truth of what Ivo fought for, and takes the first spring ferry back, unannounced. The beat is hope held at arm's length; he comes not to resume the arrangement but to ask for something realer and scarier.

chapters.title: A Songbook for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the winter ferry landing, Ivo meets Theo with the finished novel in hand—dedicated to him—and offers the whole heart instead of lent pieces. He stays; the lighthouse relights for the season. The beat is resolution: love chosen openly, family rebuilt wider than blood, home reclaimed.
